_rule: <Name> — <what it is> for <when to use it>. Plain words, no jargon, <= 90 characters, no commas.
_why: The line IS the name, because asset.name is the only per-asset free text a motion graphic has and the only text at all an audio asset has. One definition; if a description field turns out to be read, the same bytes go there.
_separator_note: The twelve components and seven caption styles use an EM DASH. The thirteen sounds already shipped with a HYPHEN in their filenames. Both parse; changing the sounds means thirteen re-uploads. Flagged for Zac rather than normalised silently.
components: PlainText — one bold line over the picture for claims titles and hard points
CaptionMatch — a line styled like the captions for quotes asides and spoken beats
LowerThird — a name above a role for intros guests credits and first appearances
QuoteCard — a serif quote with a name under it for quotes advice and testimonials
TornPaper — two slammed strips of text for punchlines reversals and before and after
StickyNotes — three handwritten notes for tips checklists and quick takeaways
EmojiCard — a big emoji over a caption for reactions shock jokes and sudden pauses
StatCard — a big number that counts up for stats prices results and milestones
Stamp — a red distressed stamp struck across the frame for verdicts myths and fails
PillCluster — a row of small labelled pills for features tools tags and ingredients
RankedList — numbered rows with time badges for steps rankings recipes and routines
Reticle — green targeting brackets with a scan line for pointing out detail on screen
caption_styles: CleanCut — plain white words for narration explainers and anything text should not steal
Cove — words in a soft rounded box for busy shots outdoor footage and low contrast
Gadzhi — one keyword lit in yellow for punchlines key terms and numbers worth landing
Lumen — a bright band behind the line for hype reveals and high energy delivery
Prime — two stacked lines in white and blue for setups payoffs and question answer beats
Pulse — the whole line fades in for calm delivery storytelling and slow reveals
TwoTone — every word outlined in a second colour for punchy loud and meme style beats
sounds: boom - deep low impact for heavy landings reveals and big claims
punchsfx - sharp hit for hard words hits and quick emphasis
popsfx - short pop for graphics appearing captions and list items
camera-flash - bright shutter click for snaps cuts and freeze frames
swoosh-sound-effects - whoosh for moves wipes and quick transitions
woosh-professional - cleaner whoosh for polished moves and smooth transitions
transition-sfx - whoosh for scene changes chapters and section breaks
iphoneding - notification chime for messages alerts and reminders
money-ching - cash register for prices revenue savings and money figures
mouse-click-sound - one click for UI actions taps and selections
shockingsfx - stinger for surprises twists and bad news
wompwomp - sad trombone for failures mistakes and letdowns
rizz - rising flourish for flirty smug and confident beats
_density_note: Matched to ChatCut's own library descriptions, which name SEVERAL moments and not one ('for shock, reversals, exaggerated reactions, key captions, sudden pauses'). Theirs use commas; ours cannot, so the moments are joined with 'and'. A comma in a sound filename breaks the upload helper's ffmpeg filter graph and leaves an orphaned status:processing asset that never resolves.
